starters_announced.note: from search summaries; the release itself was not loaded

coach_record_through.note: best winning percentage in each conference through games of February 1 names the game's coaches

rookie_challenge_announced.note: the announcement date was not found; the rosters were public in the NBA's February 5 release, so that date bounds it

replacements_named.note: the commissioner names injury replacements before the weekend; the simulation names them on the Friday the weekend opens, from closed results through the day before

electorates.reserves: the conference's head coaches, never their own players
electorates.rookie_challenge: a panel of 11 broadcasters (former players and coaches)

previous_game_coaches.note: the Riley Rule: no coach coaches two All-Star Games in a row

fan_ballot_open.note: NBA release: balloting 'began on November 13, 2003 through January 18, 2004'; paper ballots in all arenas plus NBA.com/wireless/retail partners.

starters_announced.note: Search-engine summaries of the NBA starters release give Jan 29, 2004 (Thursday); article body not retrievable to confirm.

starter_shape_per_conference.note: Fan ballot elected 2 G, 2 F, 1 C per conference ('Balloting Program').

value.voters: the 29 NBA head coaches, each voting within own conference

reserves.note: Verbatim: 'chosen by a vote of the 29 NBA head coaches ... seven players in their respective conferences - two guards, two forwards, one center and two players regardless of position. They were not permitted to vote for players from their own team.' Release dated Feb. 3, 2004.

injury_replacement.note: Commissioner rule is sourced verbatim. That the All-Star coach picks a replacement STARTER from his roster is long-standing practice but not confirmed in a 2004 source: treat that half as unverified.

value.rule: head coach of the team with the best winning percentage in each conference through games of 2004-02-01 (Sunday two weeks before the game)
value.repeat_restriction: 'Riley Rule' (from 1991 game): a coach may not coach consecutive All-Star Games; if the previous year's coach still has the best record, the coach with the next-best record coaches

coaches_rule.note: Feb 1 cutoff from the 2004 game article (Wikipedia). Riley Rule in force in this era; tie-break procedure between equal records unverified. Coaches were named in Feb 3 release.

value.name: got milk? Rookie Challenge
value.format: Rookies vs Sophomores (5th year of this format)
value.selected_by: panel of 11 former NBA players/coaches working as broadcasters (e.g. Walton, Greg Anthony, Doug Collins, Doc Rivers, Jack Ramsay)
value.game_rules: two 20-minute halves; one full and one 20-second timeout per team per half; fouls counted but no foul-outs; team penalty after 10 team fouls or 2nd foul in last 2 minutes of each half; 2-minute overtime
value.coaches: Rookies: Doug Collins (asst Byron Scott); Sophomores: Michael Cooper (asst Kareem Abdul-Jabbar)
value.mvp: fans could vote via NBA.com/Verizon text toward MVP

rookie_challenge.note: Selectors are a broadcaster panel per the NBA release of Feb 5, 2004 (NOT league assistant coaches, which is the later-era method). Roster announcement date not found: unverified (rosters were public before the Feb 5 release, likely late January).

rookie_challenge_rosters_announced.note: Could not locate the dated roster announcement; must be on/before 2004-02-05.

all_star_mvp_voting.value: panel of media members votes immediately after the game; NBA.com fan vote also counted in 2004 (weight later stated as 25%)
all_star_mvp_voting.note: 2004 release: 'NBA.com will provide basketball fans with the opportunity to have their vote count towards selecting the MVP'. Panel size and the exact 2004 fan weight unverified.

three_point_shootout.format: 25 balls, 5 racks of 5; 4 balls x1 point, money ball x2 (max 30); top 3 advance to final round

slam_dunk.format: two rounds, judges score each dunk out of 50 (two dunks in round one, top two to final)

skills_challenge.format: timed obstacle course (dribble, passes, layups, jumpers); two rounds, top two times to final

shooting_stars.field: 4 teams of 3 (current NBA player, WNBA player, retired NBA player), each team tied to an NBA city
shooting_stars.format: make one shot from each of 5 spots of increasing difficulty then a half-court shot; fastest time wins; one round

value.participant_selection: invited by the league; participant announcement dates not found

saturday_contests.note: Field sizes and formats sourced from live event notes. How contestants were chosen (league invitation) and their announcement dates are unverified; an injury withdrawal in Skills Challenge was filled by a substitute named by the league.

all_star_game_rules.value: Standard NBA rules: four 12-minute quarters, 5-minute overtime; no minimum-minutes or special scoring rules in 2004
all_star_game_rules.note: No 2004 source found stating deviations; special formats (target score, quarter-by-quarter) came much later (2020+). 12-player rosters per conference (sourced above).
